title: Jellyfish sting
summary: Leave the water safely, remove tentacles without bare-hand contact, and use nonscalding heat for pain.
sources: 2024 American Heart Association and American Red Cross Guidelines for First Aid — Jellyfish Stings
actions: Help the person out of the water without endangering the rescuer and prevent further contact.
Lift or pull off remaining tentacles with tweezers or another tool without bare-hand contact. If this is not possible, seawater may be used to help remove tentacles.
After tentacle removal, use nonscalding hot-water immersion or irrigation, or another safe heat source, to reduce pain.
Watch for breathing difficulty, widespread hives, facial swelling, vomiting, weakness, or fainting and treat possible anaphylaxis urgently.
Seek medical care for severe or persistent pain, a large affected area, eye involvement, or a child with significant symptoms.
prohibitions: Do not rub the area or touch tentacles with bare hands.
Do not routinely rinse attached tentacles with fresh water.
Do not use vinegar, baking soda, urine, or another chemical unless a trusted local species-specific protocol recommends it.
Do not use a pressure-immobilization bandage.

emergencyCall.text: Call emergency services for breathing difficulty, shock, fainting, severe systemic symptoms, or severe pain.
